text:
May envious tongues be fried in realgar* and arsenic oxide, yellow sulfide and quicklime, pitch and soot dissolved in lye made with urine and Jewish dung, boiling lead to crumble them, dirty leper-house water, foot scrapings and old clothes, asp's blood and various vipers, bile of wolves, foxes, and badgers!

May envious tongues be fried with brains of a cat too afraid of wet to fish, with rotten gums, or those of a mangy mastiff dripping rabid saliva, with pieces of a consumptive mule cooked in their own drool, in water where frogs, mice, toads, lizards, snakes, rats, and other noble beasts dip snout and mouth!

May envious tongues be fried in corrosive sublimate, dangerous to touch, on the navel of a living snake; in blood left in the barber's pots when the moon shines, one black, another dark green; in tubs where nurses scrape diapers and basins where venal nymphs wash—whoever does not understand me never went to brothels!

Prince, strain these dishes, if you have neither sieve nor screen, through the seats of dung-filled breeches, but first may envious tongues be fried in sow turds!


* Realgar, arsenic sulfide, a poisonous substance like orpiment (natural arsenic sulfide).
